prompt_bytes:
system: You expand Databricks Genie Space instructions — only the missing canonical sections.

user: <role>
You are a Databricks Genie Space configuration expert. The space already has instructions but is missing one or more of the five canonical sections. Your job is to write ONLY the missing sections — never rewrite or rephrase content that already exists.
</role>

<context>
## Existing Instructions
## PURPOSE
- Provide 7NOW delivery channel sales analytics including daily and month-to-date performance, year-over-year comparisons, order counts, customer counts, and store-level KPIs.
- Intended for operations and sales leadership analyzing 7NOW delivery performance across stores, markets, zones, and regions.

## DISAMBIGUATION
- When the user asks about "sales" without specifying a time window (day vs. MTD), ask whether they mean a single day or month-to-date.
- When the user asks about "same store" metrics, clarify whether they mean the 7NOW same-store flag (`same_store_7now`) or the finance monthly same-store flag (`is_finance_monthly_same_store`).
- When the user references "prior year," clarify whether they mean prior-year same date or prior-year same day of week, as the date dimension supports both comparisons.
- "Orders" may refer to total orders or per-store-day orders; ask for clarification if ambiguous.
- When the user mentions a geographic grouping (zone, region, market, area), confirm which level of the hierarchy they intend.

## DATA QUALITY NOTES
- The `same_store_7now` flag in the fact table and `is_finance_monthly_same_store` in the location dimension serve different same-store definitions; they are not interchangeable.
- The date dimension flags (`is_within_one_day`, `is_within_seven_days`, `is_month_to_date`, etc.) control period filtering; rows outside these flags may represent future or incomplete periods.
- The `open_status_code` in the location dimension may include closed or temporarily inactive stores; results should account for store status when relevant.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Never expose `area_leader_email` in result sets unless the user explicitly requests contact information.
- Always ensure queries against the fact sales table are filtered by a date or date-flag condition to prevent unbounded scans.

## Tables

  Columns: calendar_day, calendar_month, calendar_sk, calendar_year, day_of_week, full_date, is_month_to_date, is_month_to_date_prior_year_same_date, is_month_to_date_prior_year_same_day, is_one_day_prior_year_same_date, is_one_day_prior_year_same_day, is_seven_day_prior_year_same_day, is_within_one_day, is_within_seven_days, previous_day_flag, use_mtdate_flag
- prashanth_subrahmanyam_catalog.sales_reports.mv_esr_dim_location: PURPOSE:Location dimension table containing store attributes including geographic details, organizational hierarchy (zon
  Columns: acquisition_date, acquisition_description, area_leader_email, area_leader_name, city_name, country_code, county_name, is_finance_monthly_same_store, latitude, location_number, longitude, market_code, market_combination, market_description, market_leader_name, open_status_code, operating_system, postal_code, region_code, region_combination (+8 more)

(none)

</context>

<instructions>
Generate content ONLY for the headers listed in "Missing Sections". Never emit a header that is not in that list. Emit each header VERBATIM as given (case-sensitive for header #5, case-insensitive parser for the others — still, copy them as-shown).

Per-section guidance:

- `## PURPOSE` — 1-2 bullets on space scope and audience. If such content is evident in the schema or existing prose, capture it; otherwise OMIT.
- `## DISAMBIGUATION` — clarification-question triggers and term-resolution rules. If such content is evident in the schema or existing prose, capture it; otherwise OMIT.
- `## DATA QUALITY NOTES` — NULL handling, known bad rows, column semantics not captured in descriptions. If such content is evident in the schema or existing prose, capture it; otherwise OMIT.
- `## CONSTRAINTS` — hard guardrails (PII columns, forbidden operations). If such content is evident in the schema or existing prose, capture it; otherwise OMIT.
- `## Instructions you must follow when providing summaries` — summary-rendering rules (rounding, mandatory caveats, date-range statements). Copy the header letter-for-letter. If such content is evident in the schema or existing prose, capture it; otherwise OMIT.

Non-regressive rules (parity with proactive seeding — expand must not invent what seed would have omitted):
- Be factual — infer ONLY from the schema + existing instructions.
- Do NOT invent business rules that are not evident in column names, descriptions, or existing prose.
- If a requested section has nothing meaningful to add, OMIT its key from the output JSON rather than emitting a placeholder.

## Budget
The existing prose is 1859 chars. You have 141 chars remaining in the 2000-char cap for 1 section(s) — aim for 141 chars each. Going over will cause your output to be discarded.

Strict output rules:
- Do NOT include any `##` header not listed in "Missing Sections".
- Do NOT emit any SQL keyword or clause anywhere in the prose; SQL belongs in sql_snippets / join_specs / example_question_sqls. When describing rules in English, use verbs like "combine", "link", "pair", "associate" instead of "join"; "given that" instead of "where"; "after" instead of "order by".
- Do NOT include code fences or `###` subheaders.
- Do NOT rewrite or duplicate existing content.
</instructions>

<output_schema>
Return strict JSON. Example:
{
  "sections": {
    "## PURPOSE": "- Analytics for the sales team covering H1 revenue.\n",
    "## DATA QUALITY NOTES": "- The `status` column has mixed casing; normalize before filtering.\n"
  }
}

Keys MUST be exact canonical headers. Values are plain text with one bullet per line (each starting with `- `).
</output_schema>
